title: inula helenium subsp. orgyalis
intro: Inula helenium subsp. orgyalis, commonly known as Elecampane, is a perennial plant species belonging to the Asteraceae family. It has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties, which may help to alleviate respiratory issues such as bronchitis and coughs. The therapeutic actions of Elecampane include expectorant, anti-catarrhal, and antiseptic effects, which contribute to its use in treating respiratory and gastrointestinal disorders. The bioactive constituents of Elecampane include sesquiterpenes, specifically alantolactone and inulone, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
